I built a real-world minigolf course inside Walkabout Mini Golf

All 18 lanes of German tournament “Miniaturgolf”, at real size, playable in VR, so I can practise at home for the concrete-and-Eternit courses you find in every German town.

  • 18 standard lanes, 6.25 m × 0.90 m
  • dimensions from the official norm drawings
  • runs in VR on a Quest 3 via PC
  • built in about two days with an AI coding agent

What this is

In Germany, Austria, Switzerland and Scandinavia, minigolf is a real sport with standardised lanes. The most common system is Miniaturgolf (often called “Eternit” after the fibre-cement the lanes are made of): 18 lanes, each 6.25 m long and 90 cm wide, each with one of a fixed catalogue of obstacles. Because the lanes are standardised, a line you learn on one course works on every other course.

That makes it a perfect thing to practise in VR. So this is a mod for the PC version of Walkabout Mini Golf that replaces the scenery of a loaded course with a small city-garden minigolf course and puts the 18 standard lanes on the game's 18 holes. The game's own ball, putter, scoring and hole progression keep working.

I did not write the code myself. I worked with Claude Code, an AI coding agent: I gave directions, reference photos and corrections; it wrote the mod, drove the game itself (commands, test putts, screenshots) and compared its results against drawings and photos.

Honest status: every lane is playable and can be holed out, and the lane dimensions follow the official drawings. Several obstacle heights are estimated from photos because the norm does not give them. I have not yet measured how well VR practice transfers to a real course. The mod is not released yet.

1Getting into the game

Walkabout is a Unity game compiled with IL2CPP, so there is no script source to edit. The way in is a mod loader (BepInEx 6) that runs your own C# plugin inside the game, plus UnityExplorer to look at the game's objects while it runs.

The first plugin did three things that made everything else possible:

  • A desktop mode. A keyboard-and-mouse camera and a “putt with exactly this speed and direction” command, so lanes can be tested without a headset.
  • A command channel. The plugin reads commands from a text file (hole 5, putt 4.7, state), so the agent could drive the game and read the result from the log.
  • Screenshots. So it could look at what it had built.

2A park of our own

Lanes are built from scratch when a course loads: a playing surface mesh with a real round hole, the low side rails (“Banden”), and the obstacle. Each lane is described in a small JSON file; the plugin turns that into meshes and colliders. The original course is hidden, and hole 1–18 of the game are mapped to lane 1–18, so the scorecard and “next hole” just work.

3The 18 obstacles, from drawings and photos

The official norm sheets give a plan view of every lane with the important distances. Heights and the exact shape of the moulded parts are mostly not in the norm, so those came from photos of real courses and are marked as estimates in the lane files.

Simple obstacles (pyramids, bars, cones, the labyrinth walls) are built from boxes, prisms and lathe shapes. The moulded ones, such as the lying loop, the volcano, the wave block and the pipe hill, are generated as proper meshes by small Python scripts that sweep cross-sections along a path.

Example: lane 5, “Liegende Schleife”

The first attempt was assembled from separate pieces and had visible seams and the wrong layout. It was rebuilt as one welded mesh traced from the norm drawing and video frames of a real lane.

Example: lane 11, “Labyrinth”

4Making it play right

  • Rolling and friction. The game's putting greens are not the smooth fibre cement of a real lane. The lanes got their own surface physics so speeds and distances are plausible.
  • Lanes without a hole. On some real lanes the target is a net, a bowl or the top of a cone. The mod watches for the ball coming to rest in the target and then tells the game the hole is complete.
  • Tiny geometry matters. An exposed mesh edge at surface level kicked the ball into the air; a sharp kink at the foot of a ramp made it bounce. Edges are now buried and ramp feet rounded.
  • Every lane was test-played. For each lane the agent searched for a putt that goes in and confirmed the game counts it.

Then came two full review rounds: every lane rendered from above, from the side and from the tee, and compared against its norm drawing and against photos. That turned up real mistakes, for example an obstacle facing the wrong way round, which were fixed.

5VR

The whole thing was developed on a flat screen, so VR needed its own pass. The mod now detects a worn headset and then keeps its hands off the camera and the sound.

  • You stand on the paving behind the tee, with the lane 13 cm above the ground, like on a real course.
  • The game's putter, pointer, teleport and “Hole in one!” pop-ups stay visible.
  • Holding a thumbstick puts the ball back on the tee for another try.
  • Two bugs only showed up with a real headset: a view that was tilted away from your head, and a stutter every three seconds. Both are fixed.

On a Quest 3 through SteamVR it ran at a steady 72 fps. That was measured with the earlier, simpler scenery; the garden below has not been tested in the headset yet.

6From a parking lot to a garden

The first scenery was a box hedge, a few ball-shaped trees and lanes in three tidy rows. It worked, but it felt like a parking lot.

The inspiration for the final look is Hertzberg Golf in Berlin-Neukölln, a 1960s course that has grown into a garden: lanes parallel or at right angles to each other but never evenly spaced, lawn and flower beds in between, big old trees over everything, a little wooden kiosk and mushroom-shaped lamps.

What the garden version does:

  • Layout. Lanes stand in loose groups, each on its own pad of weathered concrete slabs, with stepping stones from each target circle to the next tee.
  • Plants. Trees with crooked trunks and wide crowns that reach over the lanes, stone-edged beds, yellow perennials, crocus meadows, hedges.
  • Furniture. Red slatted benches, mushroom lamps, a retro kiosk with a terrace, parasols and strings of coloured bulbs, a table tennis table.
  • Shade. This build of the game renders no real-time shadows. Instead, one shadow map of the whole garden is painted onto the ground and onto the lane surfaces, so trees give dappled shade.
  • Cost. About 790,000 vertices, merged into one mesh per colour. It is generated in about 3.5 seconds when the course loads; nothing was modelled by hand.

All 18 lanes, from the tee

Can you really train with this?

What should carry overWhat to be careful with
Lane size, obstacle positions and the painted lines are at real scale, from the official drawings.Heights of several obstacles are estimates from photos.
Lines and angles: where to aim, which rail to use.Speed: the game's putter strength is not calibrated against a real putter and ball yet.
You stand and look at the lane from a realistic height and distance.Real courses differ in wear, slope and temperature, and tournament players choose from dozens of balls.

So: good for learning the lanes and their lines, not yet proven for pace. Comparing a session at home with a session on a real course is the next step.

If you want to try something like this

  • You need the PC version of the game and a mod loader for IL2CPP Unity games (BepInEx 6).
  • Start with a desktop camera and a scripted putt. Being able to test without putting the headset on saves hours.
  • Build geometry at runtime from simple data files, so a lane can be changed and reloaded without restarting the game.
  • Keep the game's own holes and map your lanes onto them. Scoring and progression then come for free.
  • Work from real drawings and photos, and write down what is official and what is a guess.

Norm drawings: official Miniaturgolf system norm sheets. Reference photos of Hertzberg Golf: hertzberg-golf.de. Everything else: screenshots of the mod running in Walkabout Mini Golf.

This is an unofficial fan project and is not affiliated with Mighty Coconut or Hertzberg Golf.
